top_choice_rationale: Can Xue (P001) is my first choice on literary grounds under the common criteria. Her voice is distinctive. In the works named on the list (Frontier; Love in the New Millennium) dream logic appears to be a rigorously held formal principle that replaces conventional psychology, space and causal plot, and is not decoration. The method has been pursued over decades, and her critical writing suggests a reflective project, though the citation should rest on the fiction. The main open question is whether her consistent method shows sustained invention or repetition, especially in the long novels. I cannot settle this from the supplied descriptions, and I have not read the Chinese originals or independently verified any translation. The same unanswered test applies to Cărtărescu's later volumes. I rank Cărtărescu (P002) second: his large, patterned prose cycles are a serious and distinctive achievement, but I still cannot say whether his originality goes beyond the Romantic and modernist lineage or whether the late volumes earn their length. I rank no award (P000) last because both proposals rest on serious oeuvres, even though the corpus-coverage and translation uncertainties are real. This ranking reflects a provisional judgment on literary merit, not the first-preference counts.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my scholarly work on modern poetry, the fragment, exile literature and Celan is context only, and the profile records no personal or professional tie to Can Xue, Cărtărescu or any other shortlisted writer
